ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an 11 cm by 7 cm horizontal rectangle with two equal circles placed side by side. The left circle touches the left, top, and bottom sides of the rectangle, and the right circle touches the right, top, and bottom sides. The circle centers lie on the same horizontal midline. Reasoning: Since each circle touches both the top and bottom sides of the rectangle, each circle's diameter equals the rectangle width, 7 cm. Thus each radius is 3.5 cm. The left circle's center is 3.5 cm from the left edge. The right circle's center is 3.5 cm from the right edge, so it is 11 - 3.5 = 7.5 cm from the left edge. The distance between the centers is 7.5 - 3.5 = 4 cm.

From the text, read that the rectangle is 11 cm long and 7 cm wide. Since each circle touches both the top and bottom sides, its diameter equals the rectangle width, 7 cm, so each radius is 3.5 cm. Therefore the left center is 3.5 cm from the left edge, and the right center is 3.5 cm from the right edge, i.e. 11 - 3.5 = 7.5 cm from the left edge. The centers lie on the same horizontal midline, so their distance is 7.5 - 3.5 = 4 cm.
